text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA
- Reporteurs sans Frontieres send a letter to Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic calling for deblockade of Nasa Borba's bank account.
- OSCE has not yet received an invitation from Belgrade to monitor the September 21 Serbian presidential and parliamentary elections, says OSCE spokesperson.

- People in Serbia's northern province of Vojvodina chiefly support Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav Seselj, Belgraders for former Yugoslav prime minister and U.S. business tycoon Milan Panic, according to Partner agency poll.
- Greek government approves $10 million commodity credit for Montenegro, details of which will be agreed shortly, says Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Association of Independent Electronic Media (ANEM) says stifling of independent media continues, tax evasion used as an excuse to cover up the regime's political motives.
- Serbian Information Ministry invites all registered political organisations to a meeting on July 30 to discuss representation on Serbian television during election campaign.

- Despite the Socialist Party of Serbia's (SPS) obvious and gross political mistakes the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro is prepared to continue cooperation with it, says Montenegrin Prime Minister Djukanovic.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic calls on prime minister Djukanovic to publicly apologise to SPS over Monday's incident when protesters hurled eggs and insults at visiting SPS delegation.
- Several hundred workers of Zastava arms from Kragujevac threaten to take their protest to Belgrade on August 7.
- Commercial bank interest rates on credits nearly halved to between 6.0 and 7.5 percent, although precise data is a closely guarded secret.
- If the state continues filling budget deficits through primary issue of money, it will soon affect prices and dinar exchange rate, says Institute for Market Research.

- Yugoslav Justice Ministry says Montenegrin public prosecutor's statement that The Hague war crimes tribunal is interested in Yugoslav Defence Minister Pavle Bulatovic's responsibility for handing over Moslem refugees to Bosnian Serbs in 1992 is a drastic attack on Yugoslavia.
- Yugoslav Telecommunications Ministry begins returning equipment to radio and TV stations whose work was banned earlier. Final decision on licenses after elections.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav state and business delegation on visit to Uganda. Uganda interested in cooperation with Yugoslav construction, machinery and materials, equipment and agricultural firms.
- Serbian Mining and Energy Ministry says breakdown in Pancevo refinery fixed, supply of oil derivatives on the market to be stabilised by end of the week.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT carries 400,000 passengers in January-June, 15 percent more than in the same period 1996.
- Under a new privatisation law, most firms will decide independently on privatisation.
BORBA
- Trade with European Union in January-June reached $1.24 billion, or 35 percent more than in the same period last year, said Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Vojin Djukanovic.
- Apatin shipyard launches 112 metre-long vessel for Norwegian shipping company worth 12 million German marks.
- Pancevo petrochemicals plant Petrohemija gets 10 million mark credit from Serbian Development Fund.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- "Activities initiated by the president of Montenegro lead towards complete destabilisation of the political situation in the republic, which reflects negatively on companies' business," said Montenegrin Chamber of Commerce President and Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Vojin Djukanovic.

- "We criticise the federal government especially for its attitude towards efforts to organise a single Yugoslav market. If any function characteristic of a common state is threatened, there is no common state," said Montenegrin Prime Minister.

- "The president of the republic bears all responsibility for this case," said Prime Minister Djukanovic in response to a letter from President Bulatovic demanding that the prime minister establish responsibility of interior ministry officials for the protests against visiting SPS delegation. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
